newsitem.title: UK: Heseltine rules out British EMU policy change.
newsitem.headline: Heseltine rules out British EMU policy change.

text.p: Deputy Prime Minister Michael Heseltine on Sunday ruled out any shift in British government policy on the issue of a single European currency.

A newspaper said Prime Minister John Major had told senior Conservatives he is willing to declare publicly before the next election that the chances of Britain joining a single currency in 1999 are "very remote."
The Sunday Telegraph said Major aimed to underline his party's more sceptical approach to monetary union and to stress that it is different from the opposition Labour Party.
However, Heseltine said Major had no intention of going beyond the present position.
Asked by BBC television if Major would rule out entry in 1999, he replied: "No, he won't say that."

Heseltine added: "He will not add or detract from the statement that he has very properly made and is totally consistent with the one thing that will determine the prime minister's view, and that is the British interest.
"The issue is very, very simple. Discussions are going on about what a single currency regime will look like if it happens."
A general election must be called by May and Major is keen to keep his party's divisions over Europe under the surface as the Conservatives strive to catch up with Labour in the polls.
